corpus.title: Trump Admin To Rescind 200,000 Visas In Largest Mass Revocation Ever: REPORT
corpus.signal_text:
The Trump administration plans to revoke over 200,000 tourism and business visas for foreigners seeking asylum in the United States, the AP reported Monday.
The State Department will soon announce the revocation of B1 and B2 visas issued between 2016 and 2026 for individuals who previously were or are currently seeking asylum, according to the AP, which cited government documents. The State Department will reportedly work alongside the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) to implement the revocations.
“We are coordinating with DHS to identify and revoke the nonimmigrant visas of foreigners who have come to the United States claiming to be short-term visitors, but then file for asylum to stay here permanently,” State Department spokesman Tommy Pigott told the AP. (RELATED: Mass Deportation … After The Midterms?)
The AP noted that this would be the largest mass visa revocation in U.S. history and would likely face legal challenges.
Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau wrote in a lengthy X post Monday that Americans are “fed up” with fake asylum claims, stating that the system has “long been swamped by frivolous asylum claims,” creating years of lead time for applicants during which foreigners can “otherwise put down roots in our country.”
People in the US and all over the world are fed up with bogus asylum claims. Asylum isn’t supposed to be a loophole to circumvent immigration laws; rather, it’s supposed to provide a narrow safe harbor for persons persecuted because of their “race, religion, nationality,… pic.twitter.com/fNHbj1SsIX
— Christopher Landau (@DeputySecState) August 24, 2026
Landau cited the case of Colombian national Humberto Coral as a prime example of this abuse. Coral came to the United States on a tourist visa in 2015 and applied for asylum just before its expiration, later receiving a work permit from the Obama administration which he renewed for a decade. Landau wrote that Coral spent his time in the United States “shilling for Colombia’s far-left government” and accusing the American government of “putting people in concentration camps.”
The State Department did not immediately respond to The Daily Caller’s request for comment.

corpus.title: Trump Admin Prepares To Revoke More Visas Than Ever Before
corpus.signal_text:
The Trump administration is preparing to revoke up to 200,000 visas issued to foreigners who later sought asylum in the United States, part of an effort to crack down on what officials say is abuse of the immigration system, The Associated Press reported Monday.
The State Department is expected to announce the effort soon, targeting foreigners with B1 and B2 business and tourist visas issued between 2016 and 2026 who later applied for asylum, according to the AP. The administration says some foreigners are obtaining temporary visas under false pretenses and then using the asylum process to remain in the United States.
“We are coordinating with DHS to identify and revoke the nonimmigrant visas of foreigners who have come to the United States claiming to be short-term visitors, but then file for asylum to stay here permanently,” State Department spokesman Tommy Pigott said in a statement to the AP.
Pigott did not reveal the exact number of foreigners the State Department is hoping to target, saying “as the process will be ongoing, the number of revocations remains dynamic and will be done on a rolling basis.”
Revoking the visas would not necessarily result in immediate deportation, the AP reported. Instead, some pending asylum applications would be shifted from the affirmative asylum process to the defensive process, meaning the applicants would make their asylum cases before immigration judges while facing removal proceedings.
In an X post Monday, Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau outlined the administration’s concerns about immigrants who officials say abuse the visa system and later apply for asylum to extend their stay in the United States. Many foreigners overstay their visas and use the years-long asylum adjudication process to remain in the country beyond their welcome.
“People in the US and all over the world are fed up with bogus asylum claims. Asylum isn’t supposed to be a loophole to circumvent immigration laws; rather, it’s supposed to provide a narrow safe harbor for persons persecuted because of their “race, religion, nationality, membership in a particular social group, or political opinion,” Landau wrote.

US plans mass visa revocation for asylum seekers
August 25, 2026
The State Department is reportedly looking to revoke the visas of up to 200,000 foreigners who sought asylum after entering on tourist or business visas, in what could be the largest mass visa revocation in US history.
United States President Donald Trump's administration is preparing to revoke the business and tourism visas of foreigners who applied for or are currently seeking asylum in the country, the State Department said in a statement on Monday.
It didn't say how many visas would be affected, but the Associated Press put the number at up to 200,000, citing State Department documents and two US officials. If carried out, it would be the largest single mass revocation of visas in US history.
What did the State Department say about revoking visas?
The State Department is expected to announce the revocations in the coming weeks, targeting so-called B1 and B2 visas issued between 2016 and 2026 to holders who have sought or are now seeking asylum. These visas are generally issued for business travel, tourism, family visits or medical care.
"We are coordinating with DHS to identify and revoke the nonimmigrant visas of foreigners who have come to the United States claiming to be short-term visitors, but then file for asylum to stay here permanently," State Department spokesman Tommy Pigott said, referring to the Department of Homeland Security.
He declined to give a specific number, saying the count "remains dynamic and will be done on a rolling basis."
Officials said the revocations would not necessarily lead to immediate deportation. Most people with pending asylum cases would instead be recategorized, losing their status as business or tourism travelers, according to officials who spoke to AP on condition of anonymity.
Trump official slams visa use
Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau criticized the use of tourist and business visas as a path to asylum claims.
"People in the US and all over the world are fed up with bogus asylum claims," he wrote on social media platform X, adding, "Asylum isn't supposed to be a loophole to circumvent immigration law."
He separately alleged that the US immigration system "has long been swamped by frivolous asylum claims" and cited the case of a Colombian national who entered the US on a tourist visa in 2015 before applying for asylum.

Trump verso revoca di 200mila visti. E la Corte Suprema limita il voto per posta
Giro di vite di «The Donald» sui permessi per business e turismo B1 e B2. Stretta anche sul voto per corrispondenza
2' di lettura
2' di lettura
L’amministrazione di Donald Trump si appresta a revocare i visti per business e turismo di circa 200mila stranieri che hanno richiesto o stanno attualmente richiedendo l’asilo. Se attuata, la misura rappresenterebbe la più vasta revoca di massa di visti nella storia degli Usa e andrebbe probabilmente incontro a contestazioni legali. Secondo quanto riferito da vari media Usa, il dipartimento di Stato dovrebbe annunciare nelle prossime settimane la revoca dei cosiddetti vistiB1 e B2, rilasciati tra il 2016 e il 2026 ai titolari che hanno chiesto o stanno chiedendo asilo.
Chiedilo al Sole
La revoca dei visti non comporterebbe necessariamente un’espulsione immediata. La maggior parte delle persone con pratiche di richiesta d’asilo in corso subirebbe una riclassificazione della propria posizione, perdendo però lo status di viaggiatore per affari o turista. All’inizio del mese, il dipartimento di Stato ha reso noto di aver revocato oltre 175mila visti a cittadini stranieri dal ritorno di Trump alla Casa Bianca. Il presidente ha fatto della stretta sull’immigrazione uno dei suoi cavalli di battaglia in nome della «sicurezza nazionale» ma per le organizzazioni umanitarie il giro di vite ha violato la libertà di espressione e il diritto al giusto processo, creando un clima di terrore in particolare per le minoranze etniche.
Intanto arriva il disco verde della Corte Suprema americana sulla scelta di Trump di limitare il voto per corrispondenza, revocando l’ordinanza di un tribunale di grado inferiore che ne aveva bloccato l’ordine esecutivo in materia. Un pallino del tycoon, il quale è convinto che questo metodo «favorisca la corruzione» nonostante egli stesso lo abbia usato alle primarie in Florida una settimana fa. I sei giudici conservatori hanno accolto una richiesta d’urgenza del dipartimento di Giustizia volta a sospendere l’ingiunzione emessa a giugno a Boston in seguito alla causa intentata da 23 stati a guida democratica.
I tre saggi liberal hanno dissentito. La sentenza del massimo tribunale americano lascia comunque aperta la possibilità di fare ricorso prima del voto di novembre.
